extracted.intended_audience: Sponsors/applicants submitting NDAs or 505(b)(2) applications, NDA holders, and ANDA applicants (pharmaceutical regulatory professionals)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedural standards for submitting patent certifications, notices (paragraph IV), patent listing information (Forms FDA 3542/3542a), and related amendments for NDAs and 505(b)(2) applications under 21 CFR part 314. Includes timing, content, format, and documentation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments when a patent is removed from the list
rubrics_metrics.description: If the list reflects that an NDA holder has requested that a patent or patent information be removed from the list and no ANDA applicant is eligible for 180-day exclusivity based on a paragraph IV certification to that patent, the patent or patent information will be removed and any applicant with a pending 505(b)(2) application (including a tentatively approved 505(b)(2) application) who has made a certification with respect to such patent must submit an amendment to withdraw its certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the amendment the applicant must state the reason for withdrawing the certification (that the patent has been removed from the list). If removal results in there being no patents listed for the listed drug(s) identified in the 505(b)(2) application, the applicant must submit an amended certification reflecting that there are no listed patents. If one or more first applicants are eligible for 180-day exclusivity based on a paragraph IV certification to that patent, the patent will remain listed until any 180-day exclusivity has expired or been extinguished. A 505(b)(2) applicant is not required to provide or maintain a certification to a patent that remains listed only for purposes of a first applicant's 180-day exclusivity for its ANDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to amend certifications and submit new certifications for new patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in specified paragraphs, an applicant must amend a submitted certification or statement if, at any time before approval of the 505(b)(2) application, the applicant learns that the submitted certification or statement is no longer accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant must submit an appropriate patent certification or statement if, after submission of the 505(b)(2) application, a new patent is issued by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office that, to the best of the applicant's knowledge and opinion, claims a listed drug relied upon or claims an approved use for such listed drug for which information is required to be filed. An applicant is not required to submit a supplement to change a submitted certification when information on an otherwise applicable patent is submitted after approval of the 505(b)(2) application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claimed exclusivity — information to submit with NDA prior to approval
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant believes its drug product is entitled to a period of marketing exclusivity under §314.108, it must submit with the NDA prior to approval: (1) a statement that the applicant is claiming exclusivity; (2) a reference to the appropriate paragraph under §314.108 that supports its claim; and (3)–(4) additional information depending on the paragraph claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claiming exclusivity under §314.108(b)(2), provide information showing, to best knowledge or belief, that a drug has not previously been approved under section 505(b) containing any active moiety sought. If claiming under §314.108(b)(4) or (b)(5), provide information demonstrating the NDA contains 'new clinical investigations' essential to approval and 'conducted or sponsored by' the applicant: (i) certify each clinical investigation meets the definition of 'new clinical investigation'; (ii) provide a literature search listing published studies/reports relevant to the conditions sought, certify the list is complete and explain why those studies are insufficient without the new investigations; (iii) identify the IND if the applicant was the sponsor, or certify/provide evidence of 'substantial support' for the study (e.g., CPA certified statement that applicant provided ≥50% of study cost, or an explanation if <50%). Purchase of nonexclusive rights after study completion is not sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial certification or disclosure statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The NDA must contain a financial certification or disclosure statement or both as required by part 54 of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and copies of an original NDA (archival, review, field copies) and electronic submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must submit a complete archival copy of the NDA containing required information; a review copy with each technical section separately bound; and a field copy containing the technical section described in paragraph (d)(1), application form, summary, and a certification that the field copy is a true copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as required by paragraph (l)(1)(i), archival copies may be paper or electronic if electronic submissions meet part 11 requirements. Labeling content required under §201.100(d)(3) must be submitted in electronic format per paragraph (l)(5) (in addition to other labeling copies). Electronic submissions must be in a form FDA can process, review, and archive; FDA will periodically issue guidance on transmission methods, media, file formats, and organization. Applicants may obtain binding folders from FDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of paragraph IV certification — recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: For each patent for which the 505(b)(2) applicant submits a paragraph IV certification, the applicant must send notice by registered or certified mail (return receipt requested) or by a designated delivery service to: (1) each owner of the patent or the representative designated by the owner; and (2) the holder of the approved NDA for each drug product claimed by the patent or that holder's attorney/agent/authorized official if the NDA holder does not reside or maintain a place of business within the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The name and address of the patent owner or NDA holder (or their authorized representative) may be obtained from the USPTO or by contacting the FDA Central Document Room (Orange Book Staff). This paragraph does not apply to a method-of-use patent that does not claim a use for which the applicant is seeking approval. An applicant may send notice by an alternative method only if FDA has agreed in advance that the method will produce acceptable documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and validity rules for sending paragraph IV notice and required FDA amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided under paragraph (d), the applicant must send the notice on or after the date of filing described in §314.101(a)(2) or (3), but not later than 20 days after the date of the postmark on the paragraph IV acknowledgment letter. The 20-day clock begins the day after the postmark; if the 20th day falls on a weekend or Federal holiday, the deadline shifts to the next business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any notice sent before the filing date (or before the date described if FDA refuses to file) is invalid. The applicant must submit to FDA an amendment to its 505(b)(2) application certifying that the notice was provided to each person identified and that the notice met content requirements; a copy of the notice itself need not be submitted to FDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements of a paragraph IV notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must cite section 505(b)(3)(D) of the Act and must include (but is not limited to) specified information: statement that a 505(b)(2) application containing required bioavailability/bioequivalence studies has been submitted and filed; NDA number; established name; active ingredient, strength, dosage form; patent number(s) and expiration date(s); a detailed factual and legal basis for opinion that the patent is invalid, unenforceable, or will not be infringed; and other items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The detailed statement must, for each claim alleged not infringed, provide a full and detailed explanation why not infringed, and for each claim alleged invalid or unenforceable, a full and detailed explanation of the grounds. If the applicant alleges noninfringement and seeks to preserve the option to later file a civil action for declaratory judgment, the notice must be accompanied by an offer of confidential access to the 505(b)(2) application solely for evaluating possible infringement. If the applicant does not reside or have a place of business in the U.S., include the name and address of a U.S. agent authorized to accept service of process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice obligations for amendments or supplements to a 505(b)(2) application containing paragraph IV certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after the filing date an applicant submits an amendment or supplement that includes a paragraph IV certification, the applicant must send the notice required by paragraph (a) at the same time that the amendment or supplement is submitted to FDA, regardless of prior notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such a paragraph IV certification is submitted in an amendment before the filing date, the applicant must send the notice in accordance with the general timing procedures. An amendment or supplement seeking approval of a different strength must also provide notice of any paragraph IV certification as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation required to demonstrate timely sending and receipt of paragraph IV notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must amend its 505(b)(2) application to provide documentation of the date of receipt of the notice by each person provided notice. This amendment must be submitted to FDA within 30 days after the last date on which notice was received by a person identified under paragraph (a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amendment must also include documentation that the notice was sent on a date that complies with the required timeframe. FDA will accept a copy of the registered mail receipt, certified mail receipt, or receipt from a designated delivery service as adequate documentation of the date the notice was sent. For date of receipt, FDA will accept return receipt, signature proof of delivery by a designated delivery service, or a letter acknowledging receipt. An applicant may rely on another form of documentation only if FDA has agreed in advance. A copy of the notice itself need not be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of the 45-day period after receipt of paragraph IV notice
rubrics_metrics.description: If the requirements of this section are met, FDA will presume the notice to be complete and sufficient and will count the day following the date of receipt of the notice by the patent owner (or representative) and by the approved NDA holder (or their authorized official) as the first day of the 45-day period provided in section 505(c)(3)(C) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA may, if the applicant amends the 505(b)(2) application with a written statement that a later date should be used, count from such later date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated delivery services — definition and FDA guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of this section, 'designated delivery service' is any delivery service provided by a trade or business that FDA determines: (i) is available to the general public throughout the United States; (ii) records electronically to its database (or marks on the cover) the date on which the item was given to the trade or business for delivery; and (iii) provides overnight or 2-day delivery service throughout the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA may periodically issue guidance regarding designated delivery services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability — who must submit patent information (§314.53(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: This section applies to any applicant who submits to FDA an NDA or an amendment to it under section 505(b) and §314.50 or a supplement to an approved NDA under §314.70, except as provided in paragraph (d)(2) of this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of patents for which information must be submitted (which patents and which are excluded)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must submit required patent information for each patent that claims the drug or a method of using the drug that is the subject of the NDA or amendment/supplement and with respect to which a claim of patent infringement could reasonably be asserted if an unlicensed person engaged in manufacture, use, or sale of the drug product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered patents include drug substance (active ingredient), drug product (formulation/composition), and method-of-use patents. For drug substance patents, submit only those that claim the drug substance that is the subject of the pending/approved NDA or that claim the same active ingredient. For patents claiming only a polymorph, the applicant must certify it has test data demonstrating comparable performance as set forth elsewhere. For drug product patents, submit only those that claim the drug product as defined in §314.3 described in the NDA. For method-of-use patents, submit only those that claim indications/uses for which approval is sought or granted; identify each pending/approved method and related patent claims and, for approved NDAs, describe only the approved method(s) claimed. If the method-of-use patent does not cover an indication or use in its entirety, describe only the specific approved method of use claimed. Process patents, packaging patents, metabolite patents, and intermediate patents are not covered and must not be submitted to FDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test data required for patents that claim only a polymorph
rubrics_metrics.description: For patents that claim only a polymorph, the test data must include specified detailed technical information and demonstrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required elements: (i) full description of the polymorphic form including physical/chemical characteristics, stability, synthesis/isolation/purification method, process controls, specifications and analytical methods necessary to assure identity/strength/quality/purity; (ii) executed batch record for a drug product containing the polymorph and documentation it was manufactured under current GMP; (iii) demonstration of bioequivalence between the executed test batch and the NDA product; (iv) list of all components used in manufacture of the product containing the polymorph, composition statement, specifications and analytical methods for each component, manufacturing/packaging procedures, in-process controls, release and stability data complying with approved product specifications to demonstrate pharmaceutical equivalence and comparable stability; and (v) comparative in vitro dissolution testing on 12 dosage units each of the executed test batch and the NDA product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form FDA 3542a — required contents for original patent declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: For each patent that claims a drug substance, drug product, or method of use, the applicant must submit Form FDA 3542a with specific information and verification (subject to listed exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items include: (A) NDA number; (B) NDA applicant's contact info; (C) trade/proposed trade name; (D) active ingredient(s); (E) strengths; (F) dosage form(s)/route(s) and Rx/OTC status; (G) U.S. patent number/issue/expiration date; (H) patent owner's contact info; (I) U.S. agent info if owner/applicant lacks U.S. place of business; (J) whether patent previously submitted; (K) changes from previously submitted patent info; (L) whether patent is product-by-process claiming novel product; (M) drug substance patent-specific info (including polymorph/test data, metabolite/intermediate status); (N) drug product patent-specific info; (O) each method-of-use patent info and identification of labeling sections describing the method; (P) whether there are no relevant patents; (Q) signed verification attesting accuracy and compliance (penalty of perjury language referencing 21 CFR 314.53); (R) signer identification/contact; and (S) enumerated exceptions to required submission. Exceptions specify when some sections need not be provided if other sections already satisfy listing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form FDA 3542 — required contents upon and after approval (post-approval submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days after the date of approval of its NDA or supplement, the applicant must submit Form FDA 3542 for each patent that claims the drug substance, drug product, or approved method of use. Patent information must also be submitted for patents issued after approval as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 3542 required items mirror many items in 3542a (NDA number, NDA holder contact, trade name, active ingredient, strengths, dosage forms, approval date, patent numbers/dates, patent owner contact, U.S. agent if needed, previous submissions/changes, product-by-process status, detailed drug substance/drug product/method-of-use information including labeling identification and publication-ready descriptions for method-of-use patents, statement if there are no relevant patents, signed verification under penalty of perjury, signer contact). Exceptions to required submission are enumerated; if a declaration form is incomplete or shows the patent not eligible, applicant must submit an acceptable form within 15 days of FDA notification to be considered timely filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules for submitting patent information upon and after approval (30-day rule and correction window)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent information for patents issued before approval must be submitted with the original NDA; within 30 days after approval the applicant must submit Form FDA 3542 for each patent claiming the drug substance, drug product, or approved method of use. Patents issued after approval must be submitted to FDA within 30 days of issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant submits the required patent information within 30 days but FDA notifies the applicant that the declaration form is incomplete or indicates the patent is not eligible for listing, the applicant must submit an acceptable declaration form within 15 days of FDA notification to be considered timely filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification when there are no relevant patents
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant believes there are no relevant patents that claim the drug substance, drug product, or methods of use for which approval has been received (and with respect to which infringement could reasonably be asserted), the applicant will verify this information in the appropriate form, Form FDA 3542 or 3542a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized signature requirement for patent declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: The declarations required by this section must be signed by the applicant or patent owner, or the applicant's or patent owner's attorney, agent (representative), or other authorized official.
